llm_response.content:
COMPLETE EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN

-----------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Method: Fuzzy Regression-Discontinuity Design (RDD) around the 50 percent majority-vote threshold at annual meetings, combined with an event-time panel specification (“RD-in-time”) to trace post-meeting dynamics.

Rationale  
• Pass / fail of a CSR proposal is decided by an explicit, sharp rule (simple majority).  
• Conditional on the vote share being very close to 50 %, whether the proposal barely passes or barely fails is as-good-as random.  
• Because passed proposals are implemented only ≈50 % of the time, the design is fuzzy: crossing the threshold increases, but does not deterministically set, CSR adoption.  
• Linking the proposal-level RDD to firm-year Compustat data produces causal estimates of how being “pushed” toward CSR affects subsequent operating and market outcomes.

Why not pure DiD or IV alone?  
DiD would require identifying untreated yet comparable firms in each year and relies on a parallel-trends assumption that is less defensible given the heterogeneity in firms that attract CSR proposals. The 50 % rule gives a cleaner quasi-experiment that directly targets the research question.

-----------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
Z_i = 1 if CSR proposal i received strictly more than 50 % of votes cast (“narrowly passed”) and 0 if it received ≤50 % (“narrowly failed”).

Instrumented treatment (first stage)  
CSR_Implemented_it = actual implementation dummy (KLD strength in same topic turns from 0→1 within two years). We use Z_i as an instrument.

Control group  
Firms whose CSR proposal barely failed (e.g., vote share 45–50 %). They provide the counterfactual trajectory absent the quasi-forced adoption.

Running variable  
VoteShare_i = percentage of “For” votes minus 50 percentage points.  
Cut-off c = 0. We focus on |VoteShare_i| ≤ h, with h chosen by optimal MSE bandwidth and explored at ±5 pp, ±7.5 pp, ±10 pp.

Treatment timing / event date  
t = 0 is the fiscal year that ends after the shareholder meeting date. Outcomes are tracked annual-y (t = –3,…,+5) and daily (–10,…,+10) for market reactions.

Multiple proposals in the same meeting  
We keep only the most proximate CSR proposal to the threshold; others are controlled for via fixed effects.

-----------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
-----------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Continuity of potential outcomes at the cut-off: absent passing, firm fundamentals evolve smoothly in VoteShare.  
‒ Plausible: individual and institutional investors rarely have precise control over final vote totals; small fluctuations (e.g., attendance) drive narrow wins/losses.

A2. No precise manipulation of the running variable.  
‒ Plausible: managers can lobby, but cannot finely tune to secure 50 % exactly. Will test with McCrary density and covariate smoothness.

A3. Local first-stage relevance: crossing 50 % significantly increases CSR adoption.  
‒ Documented by prior work; will verify empirically (F-stat >10).

A4. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA): one firm’s vote outcome does not directly change another firm’s performance in the narrow window around the threshold.

A5. Implementation lag is limited and similar on either side of the cut-off (no differential timing within the window).

-----------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Remedies
-----------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Imperfect compliance (fuzziness).  
  Remedy: use two-stage least squares within the RD bandwidth (Z_i as instrument) to recover the local average treatment effect (LATE) of **actual** CSR adoption.

T2. Sorting / manipulation of vote totals (managers lobbying harder when outcome is close).  
  Remedy: (i) McCrary density test; (ii) placebo RDs at 40 % and 60 % cut-offs; (iii) balance tests on pre-vote covariates.

T3. Multiple proposals or confounding events (e.g., governance proposals, M&A).  
  Remedy: (i) include meeting-level controls for other close-call proposals; (ii) drop meetings with confounding transformative events identified via FactSet M&A and SDC; (iii) firm and industry×year fixed effects in the panel RD event-study.

-----------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
-----------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# ---- 0. Packages ----
library(data.table)     # fast data manipulation
library(fixest)         # fast FELM / IV within bandwidth
library(rdrobust)       # RD estimation
library(lmtest); library(sandwich)

# ---- 1. Load Data ----
csr_votes   <- fread("csr_proposals.csv")    # one row per proposal
compustat   <- fread("compustat_annual.csv") # firm-year panel
kld         <- fread("kld_strengths.csv")    # CSR strengths
returns     <- fread("crsp_daily.csv")       # daily returns

# ---- 2. Merge & Construct Key Vars ----
# Running variable centered at 50%
csr_votes[, vote_centered := vote_share - 50]

# Identify narrow window (initial ±10pp)
csr_votes[, in_bw10 := abs(vote_centered) <= 10]

# Create instrument Z_i
csr_votes[, pass := as.integer(vote_centered > 0)]

# Actual CSR implementation: indicator that the relevant KLD strength
# turns from 0 to 1 within 2 fiscal years
kld[, implemented := (strength_t1 == 0 & strength_t3 == 1)]
csr_votes <- merge(csr_votes, kld[, .(permno, year, implemented)],
                   by = c("permno", "year"), all.x = TRUE)

# ---- 3. Merge with Outcomes ----
panel <- merge(compustat, csr_votes, 
               by = c("gvkey", "fyear"), all.x = TRUE)

# Keep only obs with a CSR proposal in ±10pp window
panel_rd <- panel[in_bw10 == 1]

# ---- 4. Main Fuzzy RD (2SLS within bandwidth) ----
# Outcome: next-year Tobin's Q
model_main <- feols(tobinsq_lead1 ~ 1 | 0 | 
                    implemented ~ pass + vote_centered, 
                    data = panel_rd,
                    cluster = ~gvkey)
summary(model_main)

# ---- 5. Robustness Check: Different Bandwidth ±7.5pp ----
panel_rd75 <- panel[abs(vote_centered) <= 7.5]
model_rb <- feols(roa_lead1 ~ 1 | 0 |
                  implemented ~ pass + vote_centered,
                  data = panel_rd75,
                  cluster = ~gvkey)
etable(model_main, model_rb, se = "cluster")

# ---- 6. McCrary Density Test ----
rdplotdensity(csr_votes$vote_centered, c = 0)

# ---- 7. Covariate Balance ----
covs <- c("log_assets", "roa", "leverage")
lapply(covs, function(x)
  rdrobust(panel_rd[[x]], panel_rd$vote_centered, c = 0))

```
(The code assumes vote-level and Compustat identifiers are harmonised; replace variable names as needed.)

-----------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Economic theory (stakeholder and resource-based views) predicts that adopting CSR should raise intangible capital, improve employee morale, and possibly reduce capital costs, leading to slightly higher profitability and valuation.

Prior:  
• Market reaction: +0.5 % to +1 % cumulative abnormal return over (–1, +1) around narrowly passed proposals.  
• Operating: +0.3 pp in ROA and +0.05 in Tobin’s Q within two years.  
Heterogeneity: larger effects for labor-intensive and B2C firms; diminishing returns for already high-CSR firms.

-----------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (RDD)
-----------------------------------------------------------------
C1 – No manipulation of running variable …… 1  
C2 – Covariate continuity at cut-off …………… 1  
C3 – Strong first stage (relevance) ……………… 1  
C4 – Local treatment excludability ……………… 0.5 (other proposals might coincide)  
C5 – Robustness to bandwidth / specification … 1  

Average score: 4.5 / 5 → Overall design appears highly credible, with remaining concern about overlapping governance events that will be explicitly controlled for.

-----------------------------------------------------------------
End of Plan
